title: Gyeran Mari Korean Rolled Omelette

seo.title: Gyeran Mari Recipe: Easy Korean Rolled Omelette
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make delicious Gyeran Mari, the popular Korean rolled omelette! This easy recipe brings authentic Korean breakfast to your kitchen. Perfect for any meal.
seo.h1: Easy Gyeran Mari Recipe: Authentic Korean Rolled Omelette
h2Headings: Tips for Perfect Korean Rolled Omelette
seo.imageAlt: Freshly made Gyeran Mari, a Korean rolled omelette, sliced and ready to serve.
seo.imageCaption: Master the art of making Gyeran Mari, the fluffy and flavorful Korean rolled omelette, perfect for breakfast or a snack!

description: Gyeran Mari is a beloved Korean rolled omelette, a delightful side dish or breakfast item known for its soft, fluffy texture and vibrant layers. This simple yet elegant dish is made by rolling thin layers of seasoned egg mixture, often with finely chopped vegetables, creating a beautiful spiral. It's a comforting and versatile staple in Korean cuisine, perfect for any meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Egg Mixture
instructions.text: Crack the eggs into a large bowl. Add the finely diced carrot, finely chopped green onions, salt, sugar (if using), and water or milk. Whisk thoroughly until all ingredients are well combined and the mixture is smooth. Strain the egg mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into another bowl to remove any stringy egg whites or lumps, ensuring a smoother omelette.

instructions.title: Heat the Pan
instructions.text: Lightly coat a non-stick rectangular or round pan (about 8-10 inches) with cooking oil and heat it over medium-low heat. It's crucial to maintain a consistent low to medium-low heat to prevent the eggs from browning too quickly. You can use a paper towel to wipe off excess oil, leaving just a thin film.

instructions.title: Pour the First Layer
instructions.text: Pour about 1/4 to 1/3 of the egg mixture into the heated pan, tilting the pan to spread it evenly into a thin layer that covers the bottom. Allow the egg to cook until the edges are set and the top is mostly cooked but still slightly wet.

instructions.title: Begin Rolling the Omelette
instructions.text: Once the first layer is mostly set, gently push the cooked egg from one side of the pan (e.g., from the bottom towards the top) using a spatula or chopsticks, rolling it tightly into a log. Leave the rolled egg at one side of the pan.

instructions.title: Add Subsequent Layers
instructions.text: Add a bit more oil to the empty part of the pan if needed, then pour another 1/4 to 1/3 of the egg mixture into the pan. Lift the already rolled egg slightly to allow the new egg mixture to flow underneath it, ensuring it connects with the previous layer. Cook until this new layer is mostly set, then continue rolling the existing omelette log over the newly cooked egg.

instructions.title: Repeat and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Repeat the process of adding egg mixture and rolling until all the egg mixture is used up and you have a thick, multi-layered rolled omelette. Ensure each layer is cooked through before rolling. Once all layers are rolled, cook the Gyeran Mari for another 1-2 minutes, gently turning it to cook all sides evenly, ensuring it is firm and golden brown.

instructions.title: Slice and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the finished Gyeran Mari to a cutting board. Let it rest for a few minutes to set before slicing it into 1/2-inch to 1-inch thick pieces. Serve warm as a side dish with rice, kimchi, or other Korean banchan, or enjoy it on its own for breakfast.

tips: For the fluffiest Gyeran Mari, strain your egg mixture to remove any chalazae (the white stringy parts of the egg) and air bubbles. This creates a smoother, more even texture.
Do not overcrowd your pan with too much egg mixture at once. Thin layers are key for achieving the signature multi-layered roll. If your pan is too hot, the eggs will cook too fast and may tear.
To achieve a perfectly rectangular shape, use a square or rectangular pan. If using a round pan, you can gently shape the edges with your spatula as you roll to keep it as straight as possible.
